findings.evidence: Grep hits: `TensorProduct.lean:66:@[expose] noncomputable def tensorCombine`, `TensorProduct.lean:72:theorem tensorCombine_def`, `TensorProduct.lean:147:@[expose] noncomputable def tensorCoact`, `TensorProduct.lean:156:theorem tensorCoact_def`; the definitions are also marked `attribute [irreducible]`, showing downstream use is intended to go through lemmas rather than reduction.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from both definitions; keep the public equation/characteristic lemmas as the intended API, adding any missing lemmas later instead of requiring body unfolding.
findings.issue: `tensorCombine` and `tensorCoact` are declared `@[expose]`, making their implementation bodies part of the public interface even though consumers can use `tensorCombine_def`, `tensorCombine_tmul_tmul`, `tensorCombine_natural`, `tensorCoact_def`, `tensorCoact_tmul`, and `tensorCoact_natural`.

summary: The new tensor coaction API is broadly targeted at the roadmap, but it unnecessarily exposes implementation bodies for the two new linear maps despite providing equation and characteristic lemmas.
